claims.claim: Unfinished tasks do not enjoy a memory advantage. What replicates is the tendency to resume them.
claims.sourceTitle: Ghibellini and Meier (2025), Interruption, recall and resumption: a meta-analysis of the Zeigarnik and Ovsiankina effects, Humanities and Social Sciences Communications
claims.sourceQuote: We found no memory advantage for unfinished tasks but found a general tendency to resume tasks.

retiredProse.text: it keeps unfinished tasks running as open loops

retiredProse.text: open loops stay awake in your attention until they're closed

claims.claim: Crossing a doorway does not reliably cause forgetting. The forgetting is real; the doorway explanation is not.
claims.sourceTitle: McFadyen, Nolan, Pinocy, Buteri and Baumann (2021), Doorways do not always cause forgetting: a multimodal investigation, BMC Psychology
claims.sourceQuote: Across this series of experiments, we observed no significant effect of doorways on forgetting.

retiredProse.text: Step back through the door and the file often reopens
retiredProse.replacedWith: the forgetting is real, and a 2021 study across four experiments found no reliable doorway effect
